question: Question linked to image nº17 A young patient of 22 years of age is referred to us from Primary Care. He is originally from Jamaica and has been living in Spain for five months. The reason for consulting the family doctor was a feeling of tiredness. As a background, he explains some pains of several years of evolution in various joints, of moderate intensity, without inflammatory signs, which had not been studied in his country. The clinical examination shows pale mucous membranes and a painful ulcerated lesion in the leg, of three years of evolution, for which he had not consulted. I did not remember any local trauma. The analytical sample shows a Hb of 7.6 g / dL, reticulocytes 417,000 / uL, Hto 22.8%, leukocytes 13.540 / uL, with 51% of neutrophils and 36% of lymphocytes, platelets 286,000 / uL, bilirubin 2.12 mg / dL, (direct 0.4 mg / dL) and lactate dehydrogenase 318 U / L (vn <190 U / L). A basic study of coagulation is within normal ranges. The chest radiograph is normal, as well as an Eco-Doppler of the lower extremities. What type of anemia would you suspect before starting the corresponding confirmatory studies?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has pale mucous membranes" -> "indicates possible anemia" -> "Hb of 7.6 g/dL confirms anemia" -> "reticulocyte count is elevated" -> "suggests bone marrow response" -> "joint pains without inflammatory signs" -> "possible chronic condition" -> "ulcerated lesion may indicate underlying disease" -> "elevated bilirubin and LDH suggest hemolysis" -> "sickle cell anemia is common in Jamaican population" -> "considering all findings, suspect anemia due to sickle cells" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with fatigue and joint pain" -> "anemia indicated by low Hb" -> "elevated reticulocytes suggest active marrow response" -> "normal coagulation studies" -> "ulcerated leg lesion raises suspicion for chronic disease" -> "elevated bilirubin and LDH suggest hemolysis" -> "autoimmune hemolytic anemia possible" -> "but joint pain and ulceration are atypical" -> "less likely than sickle cell anemia" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Patient has low Hb and elevated reticulocytes" -> "indicates anemia with possible hemolysis" -> "joint pain without inflammation suggests chronic condition" -> "ulcerated lesion may indicate chronic disease" -> "elevated bilirubin and LDH suggest hemolysis" -> "chronic disease could explain anemia" -> "but less likely given hemolytic indicators" -> "anemia due to chronic disease is possible" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Patient has low Hb and reticulocyte count" -> "indicates anemia" -> "joint pain and ulceration suggest chronic disease" -> "but no clear signs of iron deficiency" -> "normal platelet count and coagulation" -> "anemia due to iron deficiency is less likely" -> "considering other findings, less likely" -> 50%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms of fatigue, pale mucous membranes, and a painful ulcerated lesion, along with laboratory findings of anemia (Hb 7.6 g/dL), elevated reticulocytes, elevated bilirubin, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase. These findings suggest hemolysis. The patient's background of joint pain and the ulcerated lesion raises suspicion for a hemolytic process, possibly related to sickle cell disease, especially given his Jamaican origin. The absence of inflammatory signs and the chronicity of the symptoms also support this diagnosis over autoimmune hemolytic anemia, chronic disease anemia, or iron deficiency anemia.
